title: Christian Ethics
plainLanguageTitle: Right and wrong in Christian life

sections.title: Natural law and moral reasoning

questions.prompt: Could people who have never received Scripture know that an action is wrong in itself?
questions.displayNote: Foundational  |  On entry to this dimension

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes. Human nature and reason can disclose genuine moral obligations.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Yes. Conscience or God’s activity can disclose moral truth, though I would not ground this in a theory of natural law.

choices.label: C
choices.text: They can recognize harm or social obligation, but knowing a duty as God’s moral law requires revelation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: I am unsure what kind of moral knowledge is available apart from Scripture.

questions.prompt: When a sincerely held judgment of conscience is mistaken, what does the conscience oblige a person to do?
questions.displayNote: Common follow-up  |  All readers of this dimension

choices.label: A
choices.text: A person must avoid acting against a settled conscience and also has a duty to seek its correction.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Sincerity may affect culpability, but conscience cannot make a wrong act obligatory.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The answer depends on whether the error was avoidable and whether delaying action itself causes wrong.

choices.label: D
choices.text: I’m unsure.

questions.prompt: Can an act that is ordinarily wrong become right solely because it produces a better outcome?
questions.displayNote: Common follow-up  |  All readers of this dimension

choices.label: A
choices.text: Some acts are wrong in themselves regardless of a projected benefit.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The foreseeable balance of goods and harms can determine what love requires in an exceptional case.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Duties can conflict. Breaking a lesser obligation can be warranted without making consequences the sole criterion.

choices.label: D
choices.text: I’m unsure.

introduction: Natural law refers to moral order that human beings can in some measure discern through reason and created life.
editorialNotes: Separate how people know a moral norm from what makes the norm true. BIB and PRO cover authority more generally.

furtherStudy.text: Catechism of the Catholic Church, §§1954–1960, on natural moral law.

sections.title: Relationship of law and gospel

questions.prompt: What can a divine command do for someone who hears it?
questions.displayNote: Foundational  |  On entry to this dimension

choices.label: A
choices.text: Expose sin and the need for mercy.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Restrain wrongdoing in society.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Give the believer a positive rule for grateful obedience.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Express a calling whose fulfillment depends on the Spirit’s work.

choices.label: E
choices.text: I’m unsure.

questions.prompt: When preaching to believers who feel condemned by their failure, how should law and gospel be distinguished?
questions.displayNote: Common follow-up  |  All readers of this dimension

choices.label: A
choices.text: The command exposes the failure. The gospel announces what Christ freely gives, and obedience follows faith.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The gospel both grants forgiveness and, through grace, gives power to fulfill the command.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Law and gospel describe different covenantal settings as well as different functions of God’s word.

choices.label: D
choices.text: I would distinguish their functions without making one distinction govern every passage.

choices.label: E
choices.text: I’m unsure.

editorialNotes: Keep the law’s role in justification distinct from its role in teaching believers how to live.

furtherStudy.text: Formula of Concord, Solid Declaration V–VI, on law and gospel and the use of the law.

sections.title: Sexual ethics

questions.prompt: What relationship, if any, makes sexual intimacy morally fitting?
questions.displayNote: Foundational  |  On entry to this dimension

choices.label: A
choices.text: Marriage between a man and a woman.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Marriage as a faithful covenant between spouses, including spouses of the same sex.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A committed, faithful relationship can suffice even when the partners are not married.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The moral judgment depends chiefly on consent, justice, and care rather than a specified relationship form.

choices.label: E
choices.text: I’m unsure.

questions.prompt: Does an unchosen sexual attraction, considered apart from consent or action, itself involve sin?
questions.displayNote: Common follow-up  |  All readers of this dimension

choices.label: A
choices.text: An involuntary attraction can reflect a disorder of desire and itself be called sin.

choices.label: B
choices.text: An involuntary attraction may be a temptation, but personal sin requires some act of consent.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Attraction in itself has no fixed moral character. Moral judgment concerns its object, cultivation, or expression.

choices.label: D
choices.text: I would need to distinguish what is experienced from what “sin” means here.

choices.label: E
choices.text: I’m unsure.

questions.prompt: Within marriage, must each sexual act remain open to the possibility of conceiving a child?
questions.displayNote: Common follow-up  |  All readers of this dimension

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes, each act must retain its orientation toward both union and procreation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The marriage should ordinarily be open to children, but each act need not be.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Responsible spouses may discern whether to seek children, without an obligation of openness attached to the marriage as a whole.

choices.label: D
choices.text: I’m unsure.

editorialNotes: Ask about covenant, conduct, attraction, and culpability separately. Do not infer a respondent’s personal history.

furtherStudy.text: Episcopal Church, General Convention resolution 2022-A056, on marriage and disagreement within its communion.

sections.title: Marriage, divorce, and remarriage

questions.prompt: Can a valid marriage bond end during both spouses’ lifetimes in a way that permits a new marriage?
questions.displayNote: Foundational  |  On entry to this dimension

choices.label: A
choices.text: No. Separation or civil divorce does not dissolve a valid, consummated sacramental marriage.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Yes, on specific scriptural grounds.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A church may permit a further marriage after a grave breakdown through a pastoral judgment, even when divorce is a tragedy.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Yes. Irretrievable breakdown can end a marriage without requiring a specified biblical exception.

choices.label: E
choices.text: I distinguish types of marriage bond and cannot give a single rule for all of them.

choices.label: F
choices.text: I’m unsure.

questions.prompt: Which circumstances can be grounds for recognizing freedom to remarry?
questions.displayNote: ↳ After ETH-09, if B or C or D or E is selected.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Sexual unfaithfulness.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Desertion by a spouse.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Serious abuse understood as a form of abandonment or covenant-breaking.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Irretrievable breakdown discerned through a pastoral or ecclesial process.

choices.label: E
choices.text: A distinct privilege allowing dissolution of certain nonsacramental unions.

choices.label: F
choices.text: I have not settled which grounds qualify.

questions.prompt: If a couple receives a declaration that their marriage was invalid from the beginning, what would make that judgment meaningful?
questions.displayNote: Common follow-up  |  All readers of this dimension

choices.label: A
choices.text: A necessary condition for a valid marriage, such as genuine consent, was absent at the wedding.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The church may recognize invalidity, but only under a narrower set of grounds than some traditions allow.

choices.label: C
choices.text: I would address the couple’s circumstances under divorce and remarriage rather than a distinct ecclesial process of nullity.

choices.label: D
choices.text: I’m unsure.

introduction: A judgment of nullity is a finding about whether a valid marriage came into being at the outset.
editorialNotes: Separation for safety, civil dissolution, recognition of an invalid marriage, and freedom to remarry are distinct questions.

furtherStudy.text: Compendium of the Catechism, questions 344–350, on the bond of marriage and separation.

sections.title: War, violence, and pacifism

questions.prompt: May a Christian ever take part in war?
questions.displayNote: Foundational  |  On entry to this dimension

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes, if the cause, authority, conduct, and other conditions meet moral limits for a just war.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A state may exercise force, but Christ calls his disciples to abstain from taking life in war.

choices.label: C
choices.text: No. War itself is incompatible with the peace God intends for human communities.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Christian faith creates a strong presumption against participation without settling every imaginable case.

choices.label: E
choices.text: I’m unsure.

questions.prompt: Can two Christians reach different conscientious judgments about participating in the same war and both act faithfully?
questions.displayNote: Common follow-up  |  All readers of this dimension

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes. Equally sincere Christians may rightly judge their particular duties differently.

choices.label: B
choices.text: They may both act sincerely, but the justice or injustice of the war places an objective limit on faithful participation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Christian calling to nonviolence settles the question of taking life regardless of the cause.

choices.label: D
choices.text: I’m unsure.

editorialNotes: Identify whose action is being judged. Judgments about a state’s authority and a disciple’s vocation may differ.

furtherStudy.text: Mennonite Confession of Faith, article 22, describes “practicing nonresistance even in the face of violence and warfare.”
Compendium of the Catechism, questions 480–486, on peace and defense.

sections.title: Church and state

questions.prompt: What religious responsibilities, if any, belong to civil government?
questions.displayNote: Foundational  |  On entry to this dimension

choices.label: A
choices.text: To uphold justice and religious liberty without adopting a church or enforcing a confession.

choices.label: B
choices.text: To acknowledge God or the Christian faith publicly while protecting freedom of worship.

choices.label: C
choices.text: To give a recognized church or confession a legal place in the commonwealth.

choices.label: D
choices.text: To order civil life under biblical law, including religious duties to the extent that civil authority has jurisdiction.

choices.label: E
choices.text: I would keep Christian communities institutionally separate from the exercise of political power.

choices.label: F
choices.text: I’m unsure.

questions.prompt: When a civil command raises a serious conflict of conscience, what responses can be faithful?
questions.displayNote: Common follow-up  |  All readers of this dimension

choices.label: A
choices.text: Refuse that particular act and accept the consequences.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Appeal through available legal or public means.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Organize peaceful collective resistance.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Continue in obedience where the matter falls within legitimate disagreement rather than a clear duty to disobey.

choices.label: E
choices.text: I’m unsure.

questions.prompt: Does defending a neighbor’s legal freedom to worship imply approval of that worship?
questions.displayNote: Common follow-up  |  All readers of this dimension

choices.label: A
choices.text: No. Civil freedom can be owed to a person even when their religious claim is mistaken.

choices.label: B
choices.text: No. Toleration can be prudent for the common good even where I would not ground it in an equal civil right.

choices.label: C
choices.text: I think the public authority also has duties toward religious truth that can limit such freedom.

choices.label: D
choices.text: I’m unsure.

editorialNotes: Distinguish establishment, civil religious liberty, and a church’s freedom to speak publicly.

sections.title: Social responsibility and justice

questions.prompt: A church discovers that a recurring local practice disadvantages its poorest neighbors. What belongs to the church’s corporate calling?
questions.displayNote: Foundational  |  On entry to this dimension

choices.label: A
choices.text: Offer direct material help to people harmed.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Teach the moral issue and equip members to act in their vocations.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Address the practice publicly and seek its reform as a congregation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Confine official action to word, sacrament, discipline, and care within its appointed ministry, leaving specific civic remedies to members.

choices.label: E
choices.text: I’m unsure.

questions.prompt: Can a person owe repair for an injustice they did not personally initiate?
questions.displayNote: Common follow-up  |  All readers of this dimension

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes, when the person still holds a benefit or property unjustly taken from another.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Yes, membership in a continuing institution or community can create duties of repair.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A duty to help can arise, but personal restitution requires a more direct link to the wrong.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A present duty depends on the kind of responsibility, benefit, and remedy involved.

choices.label: E
choices.text: I’m unsure.

editorialNotes: Distinguish what Christians owe as neighbors from what a local church is commissioned to do corporately.

Enter at any dimension. In guided mode, begin with its opening question, continue through the main questions in the order shown, and insert a follow-up only when its stated answer matches. After the branch, resume with the next main question. A skipped answer or uncertainty opens no conditional branch unless specified.

Choose the closest single answer unless multiple selections are invited. On multiple-response questions, an uncertainty or “none” choice stands alone. Treat unresolved tensions as invitations to clarify.

vocabulary.definition: The view that human reason can recognize real moral obligations grounded in human nature or the created order.
A person’s moral judgment about the rightness or wrongness of a possible or completed action.
A distinction between God’s commands and the good news of what God gives through Christ.
A judgment that a valid marriage bond was never formed because a necessary condition was missing at the time of marriage.
The view that participation in war can be morally permissible under defined conditions governing when force is used and how it is conducted.
The conviction that following Christ requires refusing participation in war or lethal violence, with differing accounts of other uses of force.
A person’s or community’s freedom from civil coercion in religious belief and practice.
